report:
## Conclusion: Yes — denosumab reduces vertebral fracture risk in osteoporosis

The evidence strongly supports this conclusion, based on a large, well-designed randomized trial and long-term follow-up data.

**Pivotal trial evidence (FREEDOM):** The landmark FREEDOM trial randomized nearly 7,900 postmenopausal women with osteoporosis to denosumab 60 mg subcutaneously every 6 months or placebo. Over 36 months, denosumab reduced new radiographic vertebral fractures dramatically—cumulative incidence of 2.3% versus 7.2% with placebo (relative risk reduction ~68%, risk ratio 0.32, p<0.001). The trial also showed reductions in nonvertebral and hip fractures (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa0809493; https://www.mdedge.com/obgmanagement/article/65217/gynecology/osteoporosis/page/0/1).

**Long-term extension data:** The FREEDOM open-label extension followed patients for up to 10 years and found that vertebral fracture rates remained low throughout continuous denosumab treatment, with progressive BMD gains and no attenuation of antifracture benefit over time (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8799550/).

**Independent, evidence-graded reviews:** TheNNT.com, an independent evidence-review resource, and the American Academy of Family Physicians both concluded that denosumab is effective in reducing vertebral and nonvertebral fracture risk in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis, without increasing cancer or mortality risk, though it modestly increases infection risk (https://thennt.com/nnt/denosumab-reducing-risk-fractures-postmenopausal-women/).

**Caveat:** Discontinuing denosumab can cause a rebound increase in vertebral fracture risk, particularly multiple fractures in those with prior vertebral fractures, so treatment discontinuation requires transition to another antiresorptive agent.

**Bottom line:** High-quality RCT data (FREEDOM), long-term extension studies, and independent evidence reviews consistently confirm that denosumab significantly reduces vertebral fracture risk in osteoporosis patients.
